newsitem.title: USA: Lilly's schizophrenia drug clears FDA.
newsitem.headline: Lilly's schizophrenia drug clears FDA.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday granted Eli Lilly & Co permission to sell Zyprexa for the treatment of schizophrenia.
U.S. marketing clearance for the new drug had been widely anticipated. Lilly shares were off 1/8 to 64-3/8.
The company said it expects Zyprexa, known chemically as olanzapine, to be available to consumers early this month.
Zyprexa was cleared for marketing in 15 European countries by the European Medicine Evaluation Agency on September 27.

In clinical trials, Zyprexa was shown to work better than a placebo at treating the brain disorder, Lilly said. Found in about one percent of the world's population, schizophrenia produces delusions, hallucinations, diminished emotions, low motivation and difficulty in distinguishing fantasy from reality.
Clinical work also matched Zyprexa against the most commonly prescribed antipsychotic -- haloperidol -- in clinical trials, Lilly said.

"On overall improvement of psychosis ... Zyprexa was statistically significantly superior to haloperidol," said Dr. Gary Tollefson, vice president of Lilly Research Laboratories and head of the team that developed the drug.
Zyprexa also showed fewer negative symptoms commonly seen with haloperidol treatment, such as low motivation and diminished sense of pleasure, he said.

Trials showed Zyprexa was associated with some side-effects, such as drowsiness, dizziness and weight gain. About one percent of patients in trials stopped using the drug due to non-hazardous elevated hepatic transaminase levels, or higher production of certain liver enzymes, Lilly said.
